episodes.181908: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front over Ohio and northwestern Pennsylvania during the early afternoon of August 12, 2023, and progressed eastward across central Pennsylvania through the late afternoon and evening hours. Sporadic wind damage (and one hail report) was observed with some of these storms, and there were two brief tornadoes in Cambria County.
episodes.181934: Abundant monsoon moisture surged into NM allowing for storms producing heavy rainfall and severe winds over portions of northeastern NM. Severe winds near Clayton, NM caused some damage on August 12th. Two more storms produced severe winds that were observed by automated weather stations at Santa Rosa and Tucumcari on August 13th. Heavy rainfall also produced flash flooding within the Hermit's Peak Calf Canyon burn scar during the afternoon. There were reports of debris and rocks washed across two state highways near Holman and Mora, and sandbags were deployed to protect homes in and around Rociada.
episodes.182002: Another line of thunderstorms moved through Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of August 13, 2023. This line significantly weakened as it moved into the area, but still produced enough wind to result in additional wind damage in the form of fallen trees, particularly in the Nashville metro area.
episodes.182318: A complex of thunderstorms originating in the central Plains during the early morning hours, pushed east and southeast into the Tennessee Valley during the mid to late afternoon hours. The gust front associated with this line of thunderstorms resulted in trees being knocked down in several locations.
episodes.182505: An upper level low pressure system which contained the remnant moisture from former Tropical Storm Eugene was situated off the California coast on August 12. This moisture helped fuel scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours over the Sierra Nevada. A lightning strike from one of the thunderstorms downed a large tree and started a small fire near Shaver Lake during the evening.
episodes.182958: A brief EF-1 tornado occurred northwest of the intersection of Snake Road and Reed Hall Road in Blacklick Township, Cambria County. The tornado snapped off, and uprooted hundreds of trees along a 0.32 mile path before lifting just to the west of Reed Hall Road at 8:51 PM. The estimated peak wind speed was 105 mph, and the maximum path width was approximately 100 yards. Sporadic straight line wind damage was noted to the north and south of the tornado path as well.
episodes.182959: A brief EF-0 tornado occurred to the west of Gresh Road southeast of Colver in Cambria Township, Cambria County on the evening of August 12, 2023. The tornado uprooted trees along a 0.2 mile long path and damaged a house and outbuilding on Gresh Road. The tornado lifted at approximately 8:57 PM.
episodes.183095: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust along the Martin County coast.
episodes.183223: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Custer area, with numerous reports of hail near ping pong ball size.
episodes.183229: A severe thunderstorm developed over far eastern Custer County and moved across northern Oglala Lakota County, producing very large hail west and north of Rockyford.
episodes.183230: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the Keystone area, producing quarter sized hail.
episodes.183231: A supercell thunderstorm developed over northern Oglala Lakota County during the late evening, producing large hail in the Sharps Corner area.
episodes.183233: A severe thunderstorm briefly became severe over western Bennett County, producing large hail and gusty winds near Swett.
episodes.183234: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across far southwestern South Dakota, producing large hail in some areas, along with gusty winds.
episodes.183295: An approaching cold front brought scattered thunderstorms to southeastern Massachusetts. Robust instability developed by mid morning leading to t-storms with heavy rain and gusty winds. Nantucket saw a good amount of damage as did Easton and Raynham.
episodes.183501: A frontal boundary moved through Central New York and supported multiple thunderstorms. High instability and shear supported scattered severe thunderstorms containing damaging wind gusts, large hail, and a NWS survey also confirmed a tornado in Delaware County. There were dozens of reports of trees down from other storms, with some trees falling onto occupied vehicles. Fortunately there were no injuries. There were also many reports of large hail with the largest size reported was 1.5 inches, which is about the size of a ping pong ball.
episodes.183692: Monsoon moisture over northern Arizona triggered thunderstorms that caused flash flooding.
episodes.184077: After a warm front lifted across the region in the morning, the arrival of a strong upper level disturbance and surface cold front late in the day combined with ample instability and wind shear to produce severe thunderstorms to the southeast of Lake Ontario during the evening hours. Several reports of wind damage occurred. One storm that exhibited low-level rotation as it moved in off Lake Ontario to the southwest of Oswego produced wind damage with multiple reports of a rotating wall cloud and even a funnel cloud. However, a later survey of the area by county Emergency Management officials did not reveal any signs of tornadic storm damage.
episodes.184337: A passing mid-level disturbance was the trigger for late-day and evening thunderstorms on August 12th. Strong to severe thunderstorms pressed in from southeast Ohio during the afternoon and passed through north central West Virginia. Main result from these storms were downed trees, but there was an instance of a developing funnel cloud around the Belleville area of Wood County. This was likely stemming from a tornado that had touched down in Athens County, Ohio before lifting back up into the storm. A cold front continued to encroach on the region in the evening, but after losing the diurnal heating component once the sun set, convection quickly waned over West Virginia.
episodes.184431: Scattered high-based convection moved from the Texas Panhandle into portions of western Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 13th. Sufficient wind shear and instability combined to yield a mix of semi-organized cells and clusters across the region, resulting in a few reports of large hail with initial activity. By the evening, convection organized into a mesoscale convective system (MCS) and moved across portions of north-central Oklahoma. Multiple severe wind gusts were reported as this line swept through the aforementioned areas.
episodes.184583: The combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles saw quite a bit of moisture return to the area going into the 12th. On both the 12th and the 13th, the combined Panhandles saw widespread rain and thunderstorms across the area. On the 12th some of the storms produced hail up to the size of nickels. Strong winds upwards of 73 mph were measured and several reports of wind damage were made. On the 13th the second round of storms produced hail up to 1.5 in diameter and gusts measured up to 75 mph. Some flooding also occurred on the 13th in Wheeler County.
episodes.184647: During the afternoon hours on August 13th, 2023, a weak cold front sagged southward across the area. Widely scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the front as it slowly pushed southward during the late afternoon and evening hours. These storms produced wind damage as a result of wind gusts around 60 to 75 mph along with up to nickel sized hail. Minor flooding was also reported in portions of southeast Kansas.
episodes.184672: The area became warm sectored in the afternoon ahead of an approaching cold front and pre-frontal trough. Aloft, a shortwave trough approached. This setup allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop and move through southeast NY, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184699: The area became warm sectored in the afternoon ahead of an approaching cold front and pre-frontal trough. Aloft, a shortwave trough approached. This setup allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop and move through northeast NJ, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184700: The area became warm sectored in the afternoon ahead of an approaching cold front and pre-frontal trough. Aloft, a shortwave trough approached. This setup allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop and move through southern CT, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184702: The area became warm sectored in the afternoon ahead of an approaching cold front and pre-frontal trough. Aloft, a shortwave trough approached. This setup allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop and move over the waters, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184742: A broad area of upper level cyclonic flow dominated the weather pattern on August 13th with amble moisture and cool air aloft.  This allowed for strong potential instability and wind shear in the atmosphere.  Once daytime heating occurred, scattered storms quickly began to develop across most of the state.  A few thunderstorms quickly became severe with isolated storms bringing damaging hail and winds from York to Somerset County.  In addition, localized flooding resulted from scattered showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 13th.  A very moist airmass supported heavy rainfall rates of 2 inches an hour.  This heavy rain fell over saturated ground resulting in some minor road damage in interior sections of Western Maine.
episodes.184798: Thunderstorm wind gust in Finney County.
episodes.184835: Thunderstorms moved through northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 13th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184867: A mid-level shortwave trough moved across the northern Great Lakes with a belt of stronger flow moving through the southern Great Lakes.  Scattered thunderstorms|developed through midday into the afternoon.  Forecast soundings showed some low-level hodograph curvature. Supercells evolved ahead of the cold front and create a large hail and tornado threat.
episodes.184869: A mid-level shortwave trough moved across the northern Great Lakes with a belt of stronger flow moving through the southern Great Lakes. episodes.184870: A mid-level shortwave trough moved across the northern Great Lakes with a belt of stronger flow moving through the southern Great Lakes.  Scattered thunderstorms|developed through midday into the afternoon.  Forecast soundings showed some low-level hodograph curvature. Supercells evolved ahead of the cold front and create a large hail and tornado threat.
episodes.184914: A few showers and thunderstorms developed within the warm sector of a low pressure system across eastern New York during the afternoon and evening hours on August 12, 2023. Most of the activity was located across the mid-Hudson Valley (Ulster and Dutchess counties) where thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage and some large hail. Localized flash flooding also occurred with these storms. A few other thunderstorms produced some localized wind damage closer to the proximity of a warm front across Herkimer and Warren counties.
episodes.184915: A line of showers and thunderstorms developed within the warm sector of a low pressure system and moved eastward across northwestern Connecticut during the evening hours on August 12, 2023. An EF0 tornado touched down in Roxbury, Connecticut with minimal damage as most of the path was over open field. A few trees and powerlines were also downed across other parts of the county as the storms rolled through.
episodes.184934: The remnants of Eastern Pacific Tropical Storm Eugene fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. A few produced flash flooding and strong winds.
episodes.184936: Lingering low pressure and monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. A few produced flash flooding and strong winds.
episodes.184969: A strongly forced line of storms moved across the plains and into the Missouri Ozarks during the late afternoon into the evening. As the storms moved into the region severe storms produced widespread wind damage with winds measured as high as 61 mph. Numerous trees and power lines were downed by high winds, one of which fell into a home injuring 3 residents. The storms took advantage of a very moist airmass to result in  very efficient rainfall. Rainfall was measures from 2 to 4 inches across much of southwestern Missouri with local reports in excess of 6 inches in Lawrence County.
episodes.185097: An upper-level disturbance on the periphery of the upper ridge centered over Louisiana triggered a cluster of thunderstorms over northeast Oklahoma during the early morning hours of August 13, 2023. This cluster of storms tracked along the Arkansas/Missouri state line and intensified as it encountered an increasingly unstable airmass across West Tennessee. A few storms became severe with damaging winds during the early afternoon.
episodes.185124: A continued pattern of westerly or northwesterly upper level flow produced several consecutive days of severe weather across northeastern and southeastern portions of Central Alabama.
episodes.185148: A surface cold front moved across a marginally unstable airmass across the Champlain Valley that produced some scattered thunderstorms. a few storms produced very localized wind damage in southern Addison and Rutland counties.
episodes.185225: One supercell storm tracked through several counties producing damaging wind and a funnel cloud during the evening of 8/13.
episodes.185232: Two strong systems moved through during the afternoon and evening on August 12th, with strong to severe thunderstorms producing damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.185233: A strong line of thunderstorms moved through New Jersey in the early morning hours of August 13th, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185234: A line of strong thunderstorms moved into eastern Pennsylvania during the early morning hours of August 13th, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185252: A cold front and upper low crossed the region during the 13th. Steepening lapse rates with the upper low and increasing shear along the front supported afternoon thunderstorm development across northern and eastern Maine. Some of the thunderstorms became severe...producing large hail and damaging winds. Heavy rains also accompanied some of the storms leading to flash flooding.
episodes.185443: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with thunderstorms near Key West and offshore Islamorada.  A north-northeast-through-south-southwest-oriented surface trough was positioned from central Cuba into the Straits of Florida.
episodes.185494: On the morning of August 13th a storm brough damaging wind gusts to Carrollton, MO. Then on the late afternoon hours of August 13th, a storm brough damaging wind gusts to the north side of the KC metro in Platte County.

The National Weather Service in Pittsburgh conducted a storm|survey and concluded the damage was consistent with an EF-1 tornado. |Tornado damage began along Valley View Road in East Finley township. |An intermittent, and extremely narrow damage path continued along |Cracraft Road where an attached patio roof was taken off along with |part of the roof to the main residence. Additional snapped |or uprooted trees were observed further east along the |street at a neighboring residense. The most significant damage |occurred just past the midpoint of the tornado track, along the west |side of PA Route 221 where a cluster of approximately 30 pine trees |were all snapped near the base up to approximately 1/3rd of the way |up the trees, consistent with a high end EF1 rating. Additional |damage was noted along PA 18 to a township shed and outbuilding. |This was the end of the observed damage track, with beginning and |end concident with a well-defined gate-to-gate velocity couplet and |hook echo present from the Pittsburgh Doppler Radar. Length and |times of this tornado have been updated based on the additional |damage obtained since yesterday's initial survey. The very narrow |width to this tornado is further supported by video of the event |provided to the National Weather Service via social media.

Thunderstorms producing heavy rain led to flash flooding. Up to 3.50 inches of rain fell over several hours. Garland Road was partially blocked and washed out due to overwhelmed culverts. In addition multiple culverts were washed out on Mill Road along the Garland/Charleston town line. Washouts were also reported on Corinth Road and Fernald Road in Garland...with water across other roads. Water was also reported over Kenduskeag Road and Sawyer Road near the Levant/Kenduskeag town line. Puddledock Road...in the area of Paine Road...was flooded and impassible. A road washout was reported on Bradford Road...between Main Road and Puddledock Road. In Charleston...Harris Road was closed and impassible due to flash flooding.

A brief, weak tornado formed near Ames Road, just north of intersection with Faust Road and tracked due east. It struck a shed, producing EF0 damage. Images show the debris from the shed was thrown into the pond down wind. Further east, photos show a narrow track through a soybean field north of Faust Road where it dissipated. Overall, the tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 0.38 miles. The max path width was 10 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.
